title: Continuous coefficient sheaves preserve a finite lattice sum
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology and valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ with the subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], continuous coefficient ring sheaves $A_T(U)=C(|U|,A)$ and $E_T(U)=C(|U|,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $r\geq0$, let $J$ be a nonempty finite set, and let $\Lambda_j\subseteq E^r$ admit $A$-bases that are also $E$-bases. Equip all lattices and $\Lambda=\sum_j\Lambda_j$ with their subspace topologies. The sum map $q:\bigoplus_j\Lambda_j\to\Lambda$ has a continuous $A$-linear right inverse, with the finite product topology on its domain. Consequently, for every topological space $Z$, the map $\bigoplus_j C(Z,\Lambda_j)\to C(Z,\Lambda)$ is surjective. On the pro-étale site of any scheme $S$, the sum of the submodule sheaves $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda_j)$ inside $E_S^r$ is exactly $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda)$. This sheaf is free of rank $r$ over $A_S$, and its inclusion becomes an isomorphism after extension to $E_S$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-sum-lattice] to obtain an A-basis b of the sum N and an E-basis c of E^r with the same vectors. Their coordinate functions agree after inclusion A → E: expand an element in b and use the equality of basis vectors. The E-linear coordinate map of c is continuous because its source is a finite power of E. Restrict it to N and factor each coordinate through the subtype A. This proves continuity of b.equivFun in the actual ambient norm topology, without comparing it with the explicitly recorded spectral topology.

proof.text: For each basis vector b_i use membership in the finite submodule supremum to choose y_i in the product of the input lattices whose sum is b_i. Use Basis.constr to extend y A-linearly to s₀ : N → ∏j Λ_j. Let q be the sum of the inclusion maps; basis extensionality proves q ∘ s₀ equals the inclusion of N. The map s₀ ∘ b.equivFun.symm is linear on A^r and hence continuous by LinearMap.continuous_on_pi. Compose with the continuous coordinate map from step 1 to obtain continuity of s₀. These are the explicit basis lifts of the source Pushing down by the trace paragraph. The sum q is continuous by finite addition.

proof.text: For any topological space $Z$ and continuous $f:Z\to\Lambda$, put $f_j=s_j\circ f$. Each $f_j$ is continuous into $\Lambda_j$, and $\sum_j f_j=(q\circ s)\circ f=f$. As $J$ is finite the tuple $(f_j)_j$ is an element of the displayed direct sum. Conversely any finite sum of such functions is continuous and takes values in $\Lambda$. Thus the continuous-function sum map is surjective for every $Z$, with no compactness or connectedness assumption.

proof.text: For every topological abelian group M, apply [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf], restrict along proetaleTopology ≤ fpqcTopology, and precompose by the continuous functor ProEt.forget S ⋙ Over.forget S. This gives the required sheaf conditions for all the input lattices and N with their actual subspace topologies. For any finite basis with continuous coordinates, explicitly construct the linear equivalence (i → C(Z,A)) ≃ C(Z,N) by pointwise basis reconstruction, with inverse pointwise coordinates. The reconstruction map is continuous by LinearMap.continuous_on_pi. This equivalence commutes definitionally with precomposition, hence with every restriction map.

proof.text: Each input lattice maps continuously into N by the actual subtype inclusion, so the range of its continuous-function inclusion lies in the range for N. Conversely, for every scheme object U and f : C(U,N), postcompose f with the continuous section s constructed in step 2. The components give g_j : C(U,Λ_j), whose inclusions sum pointwise to f by q s = 1. Membership in the supremum of the submodule ranges follows by finite sum membership. Thus both submodule inclusions hold sectionwise. With the sheaf property from step 4, this is the stated sheaf sum identification.

proof.text: Let d be the continuous-function coordinate equivalence for b and dc the one for c. On each U, tensor d.symm with C(U,E), apply Mathlib TensorProduct.piScalarRight, and apply dc. This is an additive equivalence from the stated tensor product to C(U,E^r). On a pure tensor, its coordinates are b.equivFun(f(x))_i times a(x). The coordinate identity from step 1 and commutativity of E identify this with a(x) • f(x), proving that this is the actual inclusion comparison. This realizes the source inverse-matrix argument using basis equivalences. All constructions use finite sums and are valid for r = 0. The sectionwise comparison and sheaf clauses are exactly the existing Lean statement; no new sheafification result is needed.
